title: Ontogenetic change in spiral angle explains narrowing-whorled and uncoiling ammonites

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Ontogenetic change in spiral angle explains narrowing-whorled and uncoiling ammonites

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In some ammonoids the spiral angle changes progressively during growth: where it increases the whorls become narrower (as in Oekotraustes), and where it diminishes towards zero the coil opens out into an almost straight curve (as in Scaphites, Ancyloceras and Lituites).

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But let us suppose that the spiral angle increases somewhat rapidly; we shall then get a spiral with gradually narrowing whorls, and this condition is characteristic of Oekotraustes, a subgenus of Ammonites. If on the other hand, the angle α gradually diminishes, and even falls away to zero, we shall have the spiral curve opening out, as it does in Scaphites, Ancyloceras and Lituites,

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XI, “The Logarithmic Spiral”; topic “Changes of spiral angle with age”. Scope: ammonoids and nautiloids with changing coiling (e.g. Oekotraustes, Scaphites, Ancyloceras, Lituites)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch11-14: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim makes explicit within-shell quantitative predictions and fossils preserve the relevant trajectory. Existing scans and standard curve analysis can resolve the pattern in the named forms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure local spiral angle and whorl breadth through ontogeny in the named ammonoids and test whether increasing angle predicts narrowing while decline toward zero predicts uncoiling. Alternative local curve models provide direct comparison.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fossil crushing can distort local angles.

Some named historical taxa have revised classifications.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim names genera and the direction in which the angle should move, and those shells are figured in open museum and atlas collections. Photographs can test the narrowing and uncoiling profiles; scans, where present, separate the angle from other coiling parameters. The sample is uneven but large enough, with standard measurements, to confirm or refute the stated ontogenetic trends.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure spiral angle through ontogeny in Oekotraustes, Scaphites, Ancyloceras, Lituites and similar shells. An increasing angle with narrowing whorls, and a decreasing angle toward an open hook, support the claim; constant angle despite those outlines, or the opposite angle trend, refutes it for those taxa.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A change in outline can reflect translation or aperture shape as well as the spiral angle.

3D scans of these particular genera are fewer than photographs, and crushed specimens distort the later whorls.
